text:
sai: Heads-up — seeing a small but consistent p95 CPU spike on host ingress when clients stream many tiny chunks (~<200B). It looks like tokenization + request parsing + gRPC framing is dominating for short msgs. Repro locally with the convo-load tool.
kevin: ok can you paste the profiler snippet you saw?

sai: sure — ran `nperf attach host-ingress` and got this hot-path breakdown (wall time pct):
```
host_ingress_tokenize        28%
http_parser                  18%
grpc_recv_frame_parse        15%
kv_cache_lookup              12%
protobuf_unmarshal           8%
others                       19%
```
The weird part is tokenization being highest even though payloads are tiny.

olivia: are these clients doing many partial sends? i.e., N small writes per request? That would force repeated parsing + decode work.

sai: yes — we simulated mobile clients that flush on punctuation. Each logical request ends up as 6-8 frames.

leo: two quick ideas: 1) coalesce small incoming frames server-side for a short window (5-10ms) before parsing; 2) fast-path for tiny payloads that skips full tokenizer and uses cached tokenization for exact-match prefixes.

ara: for (2) we'd need a low-overhead prefix hash and LRU cache. We already have prefix KV cache for prompt prefixes — maybe reuse that. But need to be careful about memory explosion.

kevin: i put together a micro-patch for coalescing at the ingress layer — gated by a config `ingress.coalesce_ms`. gist:
```
if (buffered_frames_count < 8 && time_since_first_frame < coalesce_ms) {
  wait(coalesce_ms - elapsed)
  merge_frames()
}
parse_merged()
```
Benchmarks (local, 8 concurrent clients):
- baseline p95 ingress cpu: 210ms
- coalesce_ms=8 p95 ingress cpu: 150ms
- coalesce_ms=20 p95 ingress cpu: 142ms

olivia: nice. How does that affect end-to-end latency for clients that expect immediate streaming? we can't hurt interactive UX.

kevin: we measured tail RL = +6ms for coalesce_ms=8, +14ms for 20ms. For median latency it's neutral.

sai: curious about the KV cache hits — profiler showed 12% in kv_cache_lookup. Could repeated tiny requests be thrashing kv cache state (frequent misses, populating tokenization cache)?

ara: I instrumented cache stats for the same run: tiny-frames workload results:
```
kv_prefix_hits: 12%
kv_prefix_misses: 58%
kv_evictions_per_min: 420
avg_obj_size: 280B
```
So lots of misses + evictions. Means our cache is very churny for small variations.

leo: options: increase cache shard count, increase per-shard capacity for small objects, and switch eviction policy to frequency-biased for prefix tokens. Also consider a tiny-size slab allocator to avoid overhead per item.

olivia: unrelated but saw grpc_recv_frame_parse at 15% — any gRPC framing tunables? recv window or message coalescing at transport layer?

kevin: gRPC has `SO_RCVBUF` and http2 settings: `initial_window_size` / `max_frame_size`. We can bump `max_frame_size` to reduce number of frames if clients chunk artificially. But that's only helpful if clients pack multiple logical writes into fewer frames — many clients do separate writes, not guaranteed.

sai: decision proposal: land ingress coalescing with default coalesce_ms=8, add opt-in `coalesce_mode=aggressive` for dedicated workloads, and prototype a tiny-prefix LRU for tokenization reuse with strict size cap. Also tweak cache shards.

ara: I'll prototype prefix LRU (32KB cap per shard) and run canary. Also will add telemetry for cache hit/miss per-client to detect noisy clients.

kevin: i'll open PR for ingress coalescing + tests. please review: DRAFT snippet in PR comments includes unit tests that simulate partial frames.

deploy-bot: Canaries scheduled: ingress-coalesce v0.1 -> canary group: dev-dedicated-1 at 16:30 UTC. Rolling 10% -> 100% over 30m.

perf-bot: Perf regression check queued for canary. Comparing baseline trace to coalesce run on same load. Expect p95 host-ingress CPU improvement.

olivia: let's add an experiment to see if simple tokenization fast-path (exact match cache for identical short inputs) gives big wins before investing in prefix LRU.

leo: agree. quick A/B: exact-match cache of last 128 tokens per worker with string->token array map. Low risk.

sai: owners: kevin -> ingress coalescing PR, ara -> prefix LRU prototype, olivia -> UX latency guardrails (ensure streaming delta <12ms for default), leo -> cache shard sizing experiments. I'll triage follow-ups tomorrow morning.

kevin: noted. I'll tag you on the PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingress/pull/482

ara: starting run now and will post results in this thread.

sai: thanks folks :thumbsup:

ara: post-run (10m, dev-dedicated-1, coalesce_ms=8 + exact-match cache):
```
p95_host_ingress_cpu: 148ms -> 102ms (-31%)
p95_e2e_latency: 82ms -> 90ms (+8ms)
kv_prefix_hits: 18% -> 34%
cache_evictions_per_min: 420 -> 120
```
Seems promising. I'll produce a more complete flame graph and memory profile next.

kevin: awesome. if no regression on interactive user tests we'll ship coalesce as default in next minor release.

sai: merging to alpha tomorrow if olivia signs off on UX guardrails.

olivia: will run UX tests and report by EOD. If everything looks ok, :ship:.
